history.sg_progress: The Administration analysed the data on idle equipment in United Nations entities as reported in volume I in order to determine the root causes for idle assets, and it reported its findings to the Board. It is indicated in the findings that, in addition to the justifiable need for maintaining equipment reserves at some entities for operational reasons, a large percentage of equipment has an incorrect status in the Umoja system records. Some equipment items are not properly assigned upon issuance nor are the equipment records updated by entities in a timely manner during and after the disposal process. The Administration will further increase its efforts to request entities to take immediate corrective action, where appropriate, to address the incorrect equipment records.

history.recommendation_text: The Board recommends that the Administration conduct comprehensive reviews of equipment records to ensure the accuracy of data in Umoja and take proactive measures to avoid the potential waste of assets.
history.administration_response: The Administration considers the recommendation to be implemented and requests its closure. The Administration has conducted a comprehensive review to ensure data accuracy and reduce inconsistencies. The results were shared with the Board. Furthermore, the Administration has mainstreamed data accuracy into its ongoing performance management framework through the development of a dedicated key performance indicator on data quality. In the recommendation contained in paragraph 218 of its report (A/79/5 (Vol. I)), the Board called for the Administration to conduct a comprehensive review of the data. The relevant steps have been taken and the required results have been demonstrated.
history.board_assessment: Given that, according to the most recent Umoja systems data for special political missions, there remains an equipment idleness rate of approximately 20 per cent, the Board considers the recommendation to be under implementation.
